title: Process Discovery Synthesizer
lede: Turn scattered interview notes and observations into a structured view of a business process. This workflow guides you through organizing raw inputs into steps, actors, systems, decision points, and gaps.

stages.title: Extract Process Steps
stages.description: Feed your raw notes into MossAIc and ask it to identify the sequential steps in the process.
stages.prompt:
I am a Business Analyst documenting a business process. Here are my raw notes from stakeholder interviews and observations:

[Paste your notes here]

Extract a numbered list of process steps in chronological order. For each step, identify:
- **Step name** (short, action-oriented)
- **Actor** (who performs it)
- **System/tool** (if any)
- **Input** (what triggers or feeds this step)
- **Output** (what it produces)

Flag any steps where the notes are ambiguous or contradictory.

stages.title: Identify Decision Points & Branches
stages.description: Ask MossAIc to find the decision points, branches, and exception paths within the extracted steps.
stages.prompt:
Here is the process step list:
[Paste the output from Stage 1]

Identify:
1. **Decision points** — where does the process branch based on a condition?
2. **Exception paths** — what happens when something goes wrong or an edge case occurs?
3. **Loops** — are any steps repeated under certain conditions?
4. **Handoffs** — where does responsibility transfer between people or teams?

For each, describe the condition and the alternate path. Suggest where I should validate with stakeholders.

stages.title: Surface Gaps & Pain Points
stages.description: Have MossAIc analyze the process for inefficiencies, risks, and undocumented areas.
stages.prompt:
Based on this process documentation:
[Paste outputs from Stages 1 and 2]

Analyze for:
1. **Gaps** — steps that seem to be missing or poorly defined
2. **Redundancies** — duplicated effort or unnecessary handoffs
3. **Manual workarounds** — steps that could be automated or streamlined
4. **Risk points** — where errors, delays, or data loss are most likely
5. **Undocumented areas** — parts of the process that need further investigation

Present as a findings table with: Issue, Location (step #), Impact (High/Medium/Low), and Recommended Action.

stages.title: Generate Process Summary
stages.description: Produce a clean process summary suitable for documentation or stakeholder review.
stages.prompt:
Using all the analysis above, generate:
1. A **process overview paragraph** (3-4 sentences suitable for a BRD or process document)
2. A **simplified step list** (happy path only, suitable for a process map)
3. A **key metrics suggestion** — what should be measured to track this process's health?

Keep the language clear and jargon-free so non-technical stakeholders can review it.

whatYouNeed: Interview notes, observation logs, or free-text descriptions of the current process
Names of the systems or tools involved (if known)
Any existing process documentation (even outdated versions help)
expectedOutput: A structured process document with steps, actors, systems, decision points, gaps analysis, and a clean summary — ready for stakeholder validation or as input to a formal process map.
remember: Always remove confidential details before prompting. Review every AI output — you own the final deliverable.

title: Stakeholder Analysis Accelerator
lede: A repeatable workflow that combines MossAIc with proven BA practice to map who matters, what they need, and how to engage them — in about 15 minutes instead of hours.

stages.title: Identify & Categorize
stages.description: List your known stakeholders and ask MossAIc to suggest missing roles based on the project type.
stages.prompt:
I am a Business Analyst starting stakeholder analysis for [project name/description]. Here are the stakeholders I have identified so far:
[List names/roles]

Suggest additional stakeholder roles I may be missing based on this type of initiative. For each suggestion, explain why they should be included.

stages.title: Map Influence & Interest
stages.description: For each stakeholder, assess their level of influence over the project and their level of interest in its outcome.
stages.prompt:
Here is my stakeholder list for [project name]:
[Full stakeholder list]

For each stakeholder, assess:
- **Influence** (High/Medium/Low) — their power to affect project decisions
- **Interest** (High/Medium/Low) — how much the outcome affects them
- **Disposition** (Champion / Supporter / Neutral / Resistant)

Present as a table and recommend a quadrant placement (Manage Closely / Keep Satisfied / Keep Informed / Monitor).

stages.title: Plan Engagement
stages.description: Generate a tailored engagement approach for each stakeholder based on their quadrant placement.
stages.prompt:
Based on this stakeholder analysis:
[Paste the table from Stage 2]

For each stakeholder, recommend:
1. **Communication frequency** (weekly, biweekly, monthly, as-needed)
2. **Preferred format** (1:1 meeting, email update, steering committee, workshop)
3. **Key message focus** — what matters most to this person
4. **Risk to manage** — what could go wrong if this stakeholder is under-engaged

Present as an engagement plan table I can include in my project documentation.

whatYouNeed: A project name or initiative description
A rough list of stakeholder names or roles (even partial is fine)
Any known concerns, priorities, or political dynamics
expectedOutput: A stakeholder register with influence/interest mapping and a tailored engagement plan — ready to drop into your project documentation or share with your project manager.
remember: Always remove confidential details before prompting. Review every AI output — you own the final deliverable.

title: UAT Scenario Builder
lede: Draft business-focused user acceptance test scenarios directly from approved requirements, so testing validates what the business actually asked for — not just what was built.

stages.title: Generate Happy-Path Scenarios
stages.description: Start with the core scenarios that validate the primary requirements under normal conditions.
stages.prompt:
I am a Business Analyst creating UAT scenarios. Here are the approved requirements:

[Paste requirements or user stories with acceptance criteria]

For each requirement, generate UAT test scenarios that cover the happy path (normal, expected usage). For each scenario include:
- **Scenario ID** (e.g., UAT-001)
- **Scenario name**
- **User role** performing the test
- **Preconditions**
- **Step-by-step actions** (written from the user's perspective, not technical)
- **Expected result**

Write in business language that a non-technical tester can follow.

stages.title: Add Edge Cases & Negative Tests
stages.description: Expand coverage with boundary conditions, error scenarios, and exception paths.
stages.prompt:
Here are the happy-path UAT scenarios:
[Paste output from Stage 1]

Now generate additional scenarios for:
1. **Boundary conditions** — minimum/maximum values, empty fields, character limits
2. **Error handling** — what happens when the user does something unexpected?
3. **Business rule validation** — scenarios that test specific business rules or constraints
4. **Permission/role-based tests** — what should different user roles see or not see?
5. **Data scenarios** — edge cases in data (duplicates, special characters, large volumes)

Use the same format as the happy-path scenarios. Flag which requirement each scenario traces back to.

stages.title: Build the Test Execution Sheet
stages.description: Compile everything into a structured test execution format ready for UAT testers.
stages.prompt:
Combine all UAT scenarios into a test execution sheet with these columns:

| Scenario ID | Requirement | Scenario Name | User Role | Preconditions | Steps | Expected Result | Pass/Fail | Tester | Date | Notes |

Also generate:
1. A **UAT summary** — total scenarios, coverage by requirement, and any requirements with no test coverage
2. **Entry criteria** — what must be true before UAT can begin
3. **Exit criteria** — what defines a successful UAT round

Format the scenarios so they can be pasted directly into a spreadsheet.

whatYouNeed: Approved requirements or user stories with acceptance criteria
Knowledge of the key user roles who will perform UAT
Any known business rules, edge cases, or constraints
expectedOutput: A complete UAT test suite with happy-path scenarios, edge cases, and a ready-to-use test execution sheet — traceable back to the original requirements.
remember: Always remove confidential details before prompting. Review every AI output — you own the final deliverable.
